title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. 𝔖^+ = SL(2,Z), presented as ⟨ρ,σ | ρ^6 = σ^4 = 1, ρ^3 = σ^2⟩ (the amalgam Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6). 𝔖^{+∧} is its profinite completion. Π = 𝔖^+[2] = Γ(2) is the kernel of reduction to SL(2,Z/2) ≅ S_3. Γ(2) = {±1} × F_2, and Γ(2)/±1 ≅ π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) = Π_{0,3}. Also 𝔖^{+∧}/{±1} = PSL(2,Z)^ ≅ 𝔖_{0,3}^∧, the extension of S_3 by π̂_{0,3}; this is the orbifold π_1 of M_{1,1} = (P^1−3 pts)/S_3. ε_0 = σρ is the parabolic generator, with L_0^𝔖 = ε_0^{Ẑ}. ℓ_0 = ε_0^2 lies in Π, with L_0^Π = ℓ_0^{Ẑ}.

Previous page. The abelianization of SL(2,Z)^ is Z/12, so there is a unique nontrivial character sg to {±1}; it is the sign of S_3. Since −1 is central, Θ(x) = x·sg(x) is an automorphism of 𝔖^{+∧}. It acts trivially on PSL(2,Z)^ and is the only nontrivial such lift. Θ(ε_0) = −ε_0 because sg(σρ) = −1.

Top of this page. −ε_0 is not conjugate to any ε_0^μ (μ ∈ Ẑ*). One sees this already in SL(2,Ẑ): the trace of −ε_0 is −2, while the trace of ε_0^μ is 2. Thus Θ does not send L_0^𝔖 to a conjugate of itself. By contrast, (12) Θ(ℓ_0) = ℓ_0, since ℓ_0 lies in Π = ker sg, so Θ(L_0^Π) = L_0^Π.

Proposition. Consider the map (3) M_{0,3}^~ → Aut(𝔖^{+∧}). Here M_{0,3}^~ is Grothendieck's group of automorphisms of 𝔖_{0,3}^∧ that stabilize π̂_{0,3} and send the inertia ξ_0 to a conjugate of ξ_0^μ (μ ∈ Ẑ*); it is a 'Teichmüller/GT-type' group. The map (3) is injective, and its image consists exactly of the automorphisms u with:
(a) u stabilizes Π^∧ = 𝔖^{+∧}[2], the kernel of the map to SL(2,Z/2);
(b) u(ε_0) = int(f_0^{-1})(ε_0^μ) for some μ ∈ Ẑ* and some f_0.

Proof. Injectivity was already shown. Necessity of (a) is trivial: Π^∧ is the inverse image of π̂_{0,3}. For (b), reduce to M_{0,3}^~[0], where u_0(ξ_0) = ξ_0^μ by construction of N_{1,1}^~ from M_{0,3}^~.

Sufficiency (next page). u descends to ũ on PSL(2,Z)^ = 𝔖_{0,3}^∧ satisfying the defining conditions of M_{0,3}^~. Its canonical lift u' then differs from u by an automorphism trivial on PSL^. Such an automorphism is either 1 or Θ, and Θ is excluded by (b) via the ε_0 vs −ε_0 computation. Hence u = u'.

Purpose. This identifies Grothendieck's 'M_{0,3} ⇒ N_{1,1}' lifting of the Teichmüller-type group to genus one: profinite SL(2,Z) is the profinite π_1 of the moduli stack M_{1,1}. The page characterizes the M_{0,3}^~-action intrinsically inside Aut(SL(2,Z)^), using the central ±1 and the unique sign character.
errors: No substantive error. The non-conjugacy of ε_0 and −ε_0 is correctly checked through the image in SL(2,Ẑ) (trace 2 vs −2). This is legitimate even though SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ) is not injective (no congruence subgroup property), since non-conjugacy in a quotient implies non-conjugacy upstairs.

The page leaves implicit that Hom(𝔖^{+∧}, {±1}) has a single nontrivial element (shown on the previous page via abelianization Z/12). It also leaves implicit that every automorphism inducing the identity mod the center ±1 has the form x ↦ x·χ(x); this holds because ±1 is central of order 2. Both are fine.

ideas.what: Automorphisms of profinite SL(2,Z) acting trivially on PSL(2,Z)^ are given by the sign character; the unique nontrivial one, Θ(x) = x·sg(x), sends the parabolic ε_0 to −ε_0, which is not a conjugate of a power of ε_0.
ideas.modern_name: central twist by a character; lifting automorphisms from PSL_2 to SL_2

ideas.what: Characterization of the image of the Teichmüller-type group M_{0,3}^~ in Aut(SL(2,Z)^) as the automorphisms preserving Γ(2)^ and preserving the inertia (parabolic) subgroup up to conjugacy and power.
ideas.modern_name: inertia-preserving automorphism groups of profinite π_1(M_{1,1}) vs π_1(M_{0,3}); action of GT/Teichmüller-type groups on profinite genus-one mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (GT acting on Γ̂_{1,1}); Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki and Minamide–Nakamura (automorphism groups of profinite braid / configuration space groups)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower and the genus-1 two-level principle, not this statement

missed.claim: An explicit, intrinsic description, with complete proof, of how Grothendieck's group M_{0,3}^~ sits inside Aut(SL(2,Z)^): exactly the automorphisms stabilizing the level-2 congruence subgroup and sending the parabolic subgroup to a conjugate. The ±1 lifting ambiguity is resolved by the sign character Θ.
missed.quote: L'homom (3) M_{0,3}^~ → Aut(Ŝ^+) est injectif, et son image est formée des automorphismes u de Ŝ^+ qui satisfont les deux conditions suivantes a) u stabilise Π^∧ = S^{+∧}[2] ... b) u transforme L_0^S en un sous-groupe ... conjugué de L_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early (1980s) version of results later obtained on GT-type and inertia-preserving automorphisms of profinite π_1(M_{1,1}) (Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki, Minamide–Nakamura). It is of historical interest, but the mathematics is likely subsumed by that later literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, complete proposition from the unpublished genus-0 to genus-1 passage of the Longue Marche follow-up, predating the published treatments of GT acting on profinite SL_2(Z) / M_{1,1}. The content itself is fairly elementary given the setup and overlaps with later known results.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 is largely illegible. 'hors de doute' is a guess; the crossed-out fraction above 𝔖_{0,3}^/Π_{0,3}^ is unreadable.

In 'qui ne doit avoir μ=1' the parse is uncertain. The sense seems to be that ℓ_0 = ε_0^2 is conjugate to ℓ_0^μ only with μ = 1 when coming from −ε_0. The bracket closing '... ]' ends a parenthetical begun on p. 573.
The handwriting has 'Sl(2, Ẑ)'' with a prime; the prime may denote the derived/commutator subgroup or another variant of SL(2,Ẑ).
The handwritten page number '591' is Grothendieck's own pagination; 574 is the archive numbering.
